items.title: Library supplement: Coordinate sphere gradient

source.attribution: Generic exposition of classical sphere calculus; no primary-textbook completion or novelty claim.

items.statement: Write \(E_n=\mathbb R^{n+1}\), \(S_n=\{x\in E_n:\|x\|=1\}\), and \(M_{n,N}=S_n^{\operatorname{Fin}N}\). The dimensions are natural numbers and may be zero. For every natural \(n,N\), every real function \(f:M_{n,N}\to\mathbb R\), every coordinate \(i\in\operatorname{Fin}N\), and every configuration \(x\), fix the other coordinates and apply the total sphere-gradient definition to the section \(y\mapsto f(x[i\leftarrow y])\) at \(x_i\). No regularity is part of the definition. Under joint intrinsic C¹ regularity it is the ordinary coordinate intrinsic gradient. For \(N=0\) there is no coordinate argument. The configuration \(x[i\leftarrow y]\) replaces coordinate \(i\) of \(x\) by \(y\) and leaves every other coordinate fixed. For \(g:S_n\to\mathbb R\), define \(g^{\mathrm r}(z)=g(\|z\|^{-1}z)\) for \(z\ne0\), with \(g^{\mathrm r}(0)=0\), and \(\nabla_S^{\mathrm{tot}}g(u)=P_u\mathcal R^{-1}(D_{\mathrm{tot}}g^{\mathrm r}(u))\). Here \(P_uv=v-\langle u,v\rangle u\), \(\mathcal R^{-1}\) is the inverse real Euclidean Riesz isometry, and \(D_{\mathrm{tot}}\) is the ordinary Fréchet derivative where it exists and zero otherwise. Joint intrinsic C¹ refers to the ordinary finite product of the stereographic sphere smooth structures.
assumptions: Use the indicated canonical real Euclidean, unit-sphere and finite-product carriers; no positive-dimension restriction is imposed.
This is a definition or abbreviation. It imposes no unstated regularity, tangency, integrability or probability hypothesis.
